claim.qualifier: Lucid prominently advertises 'up to 516 mi range' across marketing surfaces. The 516 figure applies only to 19-inch aero-optimized wheels.
claim.verbatim_quote: Lucid Air Grand Touring AWD (19") — 516 miles EPA combined

sources.name: Lucid — Air marketing and configurator pages

reality.qualifier: EPA range for Grand Touring with 21-inch wheels is 469 mi — a 47-mile range cliff for choosing the larger wheel option, which many GT buyers select for visual reasons.
reality.verbatim_quote: Grand Touring (19") — 516 mi … Grand Touring (21") — 469 mi

sources.name: Recharged — Lucid Air real-world range tables

narrative_one_liner: Lucid markets 'up to 516 mi'; choosing 21in wheels (popular cosmetic upgrade) drops EPA range to 469 mi — a 47-mile cliff.
narrative: Lucid Air Grand Touring's headline 516 mi range applies only to the 19-inch aero-optimized wheel configuration. Buyers selecting the more visually preferred 21-inch wheels lose 47 mi of EPA range (516 → 469 mi). The headline figure is what marketing emphasizes; the wheel-size cliff is documented in fine print but rarely featured. This is similar to other manufacturers (Tesla Model Y 311 mi vs 327 mi by wheel) but the magnitude in the Lucid case is among the largest in our dataset.
methodology_notes: Both numbers are EPA-certified values; the deception is in marketing salience, not measurement.
caveats: EPA-certified at both sizes; both are valid range estimates.
Lucid's configurator does display range per wheel choice when buyer selects; deception is in pre-configurator marketing.
47-mile cliff in absolute terms is large; in percentage terms (9%) it is similar to other EVs.
alternative_explanations: Aero penalty on wider/larger wheels is genuine engineering; this is not deception in any moral sense.
Buyers who care about range can choose the 19in wheels and get the headline number; choice is preserved.
